title: Haze4K development bounded local-action oracle
rationale: The fixed official Haze4K ConvIR-B exhibited strict local errors repeatable across at least three of four haze variants in 50/100 isolated development scenes, with a Wilson lower bound of 0.4038. This authorizes one non-deployable oracle, not module design. The oracle freezes the residual-scale actions weaken 0.8, keep 1.0, and strengthen 1.2. Its decisive contrast is deliberately stringent: a GT-selected 32-pixel spatial action field must beat a GT-selected per-image best uniform action drawn from the identical bounded set. This isolates spatial selection headroom from ordinary whole-image strength calibration. Candidate-confirmation data, training, proxy fitting, and structure selection remain prohibited.

scientific_contract.question: On the isolated 100-scene Haze4K official-test development partition, does a GT-privileged 32-pixel spatial oracle over bounded residual scales 0.8, 1.0, and 1.2 have material and safe scene-level restoration headroom beyond a GT-privileged per-image best uniform action over the identical set?

intervention.primary_variable: GT-selected per-tile bounded residual scale versus GT-selected per-image best uniform residual scale
intervention.reference: per-image best uniform action selected using GT from the identical weaken 0.8, keep 1.0, and strengthen 1.2 action set
intervention.matched_budget: one frozen official ConvIR-B inference per each of 400 nested variants; all uniform and spatial actions derive from that same prediction with zero training
fixed_factors: only the isolated 100-scene development_screening asset is delivered; the 150-scene candidate_confirmation asset is absent
official ConvIR-B base graph with 8,630,665 frozen parameters and strict checkpoint load
action formula clip(hazy + scale times (official_prediction minus hazy), 0, 1)
action set weaken scale 0.8, keep scale 1.0, strengthen scale 1.2
uniform reference uses GT to select the lowest-RGB-MSE whole-image action separately for each haze variant
spatial oracle uses GT to select the lowest-RGB-MSE action independently for each origin-aligned 32-pixel tile
right and bottom boundary tiles score valid image pixels only and are never counted as independent groups
four nested variants are averaged within canonical clear scene before equal-weight scene inference
RGB MSE defines oracle actions; PSNR is primary utility, RGB SSIM and mean absolute channel-bias are safety metrics
20,000 paired scene bootstrap resamples with seed 20260725

primary_estimand.metric: joint evidence that the paired scene-mean spatial-minus-best-uniform delta PSNR 95 percent bootstrap lower bound is at least 0.10 dB and the Wilson lower bound for scenes gaining at least 0.10 dB is at least 0.20
primary_estimand.aggregation: compute variant delta PSNR, average four variants within canonical clear scene, then equal-weight paired inference across 100 scenes

controls: official ConvIR-B keep output with no action
GT-selected per-image best uniform action from the identical bounded set
deterministic inclusion of keep guarantees the uniform oracle cannot have higher RGB MSE than the official output
complete per-tile enumeration guarantees the spatial oracle cannot have higher RGB MSE than the best uniform oracle
synthetic manufactured heterogeneous residual requiring both weaken and strengthen actions
synthetic SSIM identity, bootstrap direction, finite finalizer, and spatial-dominance references
strict scene-level aggregation; variants, tiles, pixels, and clear aliases never count as independent groups

uncertainty.method: paired 20,000-resample bootstrap over canonical scenes for mean delta PSNR and two-sided 95 percent Wilson intervals for material-benefit and harm prevalences

gates.estimand: exact parent authorization, isolated 100-scene role, 400 finite inferences and oracle finalizations, no candidate-confirmation asset, and no training
lower 95 percent scene-bootstrap bound for spatial-minus-best-uniform delta PSNR in dB
lower 95 percent Wilson bound for scenes with mean spatial-minus-best-uniform delta PSNR at least 0.10 dB
upper 95 percent Wilson bound for scenes whose mean spatial-minus-uniform RGB SSIM is at most -0.005
upper 95 percent Wilson bound for scenes whose mean spatial-minus-uniform absolute RGB channel-bias is at least 1/255

scientific_contract.competing_explanation: Any positive result may be specific to GT-optimized RGB-MSE residual rescaling, the three chosen scales, 32-pixel hard tiles, clipping, synthetic Haze4K content, or official-checkpoint calibration; it does not establish deployable action prediction, perceptual optimality, physical haze causality, or superiority of a future network module.
disabled_actions: delivering or accessing the 150-scene candidate-confirmation asset
training, proxy fitting, structure selection, threshold adaptation, action-set adaptation, or module design
claiming the GT oracle is deployable or that oracle actions are available from the input
claiming the frozen three-action family is globally optimal over other action spaces or insertion positions
claiming RGB-MSE oracle headroom proves perceptual improvement or a physical haze mechanism
treating variants, tiles, pixels, or clear aliases as independent statistical units
automatically continuing into proxy prediction, module work, confirmation, or NH-HAZE

precision_contract.rationale: All 100 independent development scenes are used. The worst-case 95 percent prevalence half-width target 0.098 requires 100 scenes and applies to the decisive material-benefit and harm prevalence gates; four variants remain nested.

capability.production_path_statement: The exact official Haze4K ConvIR-B graph is strict-loaded and frozen, followed by the exact production uniform and 32-pixel spatial bounded-action enumeration, RGB MSE/PSNR, RGB SSIM, color-bias, scene aggregation, Wilson, bootstrap, and terminal finalizer paths on a device-aware no-data fixture.

precision.source_reference: Worst-case Bernoulli standard deviation 0.5 fixed analytically; all 100 canonical development scenes are used and four haze variants do not increase independent n.
